'''Jerry Allen Coyne''' (born December 30, 1949)<ref name=":1">{{cite web | last= Coyne| first= Jerry| title= Monday: Hili dialogue (and Leon monologue)|url=https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2019/12/30/monday-hili-dialogue-and-leon-monologue-32/| date= December 30, 2019| website= Why Evolution is True, WordPress | access-date= December 9, 2020| quote=  Notables born on this day include: [...] 1949 – Jerry Coyne, superannuated evolutionary biologist, your host. }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last= Garg | first= Anu | title= Humdinger |url=https://wordsmith.org/words/humdinger.html| date= December 30, 2019| website= A.Word.A.Day, Wordsmith.org| access-date= December 9, 2020 }}</ref> is an American [[biologist]] and [[Skepticism|skeptic]] known for his work on [[speciation]] and his commentary on [[intelligent design]].  A professor emeritus of ecology and evolution at the [[University of Chicago]], he has published on the theory of [[evolution]]. His concentration is speciation and [[Ecological genetics|ecological]] and [[evolutionary genetics]], particularly as they involve the fruit fly, ''[[Drosophila]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.edge.org/memberbio/jerry_coyne |title=Jerry Coyne |year=2013 |publisher=[[Edge.org]] |access-date=January 24, 2014}}</ref> In 2023 he became a fellow with the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Committee for Skeptical Inquiry Elects Twelve New CSI Fellows |url=https://centerforinquiry.org/news/committee-for-skeptical-inquiry-elects-twelve-new-csi-fellows/ |website=centerforinquiry.net |date=December 18, 2023 |publisher=Center for Inquiry |access-date=21 December 2023}}</ref>

He is the author of the text ''Speciation'' and the bestselling non-fiction book ''[[Why Evolution is True|Why Evolution Is True]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Best Sellers Hardcover Nonfiction|journal=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/best-sellers-books/2009-02-22/hardcover-nonfiction/list.html|access-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref>  Coyne maintains a website and writes for his blog, also called ''Why Evolution Is True''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coyne|first=Jerry|title=Why Evolution Is True|url=http://jerrycoyne.uchicago.edu/index.html|publisher=Jerry Coyne|access-date=January 25, 2014|archive-date=August 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805021458/http://jerrycoyne.uchicago.edu/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a [[hard determinist]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=List |first=Christian |date=February 6, 2020 |title=Science Hasn't Refuted Free Will |url=https://www.bostonreview.net/articles/christian-list-has-science-refuted-free-will/ |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=[[Boston Review]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Coyne gained attention outside of the scientific community as a public critic of religion. As a proponent of [[New Atheism]],<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Berezow |first=Alex |title=Jerry Coyne's Twisted History of Science and Religion |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexberezow/2013/10/21/jerry-coynes-twisted-history-of-science-religion/ |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> he is often cited with atheists such as [[Richard Dawkins]] and [[Sam Harris]]. He is the author of the book ''[[Faith Versus Fact]]''.<ref name=Maroon2018/>

== Early life and education ==
Jerry Allen Coyne was born December 30, 1949.<ref name=":1" /> He was raised by Jewish parents.<ref name=":2" /> He graduated with a B.S. in biology from the [[College of William & Mary]] in 1971, receiving the [[Botetourt Medal]] for academic achievement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scrc-kb.libraries.wm.edu/botetourt-medal|title=Botetourt Medal|work=Special Collections Research Center Knowledgebase|date=September 9, 2019 |publisher=[[Earl Gregg Swem Library]], [[College of William & Mary]]|location=[[Williamsburg, Virginia|Williamsburg]], [[Virginia|VA]]|access-date=February 11, 2025}}</ref> According to Coyne, while in college, he was involved in activism against [[apartheid]] and protested against the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name="Maroon2018" /> His graduate work at [[Rockefeller University]] under [[Theodosius Dobzhansky]] was interrupted when he was drafted.{{Clarify|reason=into what? when?|date=November 2022}}  He earned a Ph.D. in biology at [[Harvard University]] in 1978, studying under [[Richard Lewontin]], and went on to do a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[University of California, Davis]], with Timothy Prout.{{Citation needed|date=November 2022}}

== Career ==
Coyne was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1988.<ref name="CoyneGuggen">{{cite web |title=Jerry A. Coyne |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/jerry-a-coyne/ |website=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]] |access-date=January 19, 2023 |archive-date=January 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230119044701/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/jerry-a-coyne/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2007.<ref name="AAAS2007">{{cite web |title=Professor Jerry Allen Coyne |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/jerry-allen-coyne |website=[[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] |access-date=January 19, 2023}}</ref> He received the [[Freedom From Religion Foundation#Events and activities|Emperor Has No Clothes Award]] from the [[Freedom from Religion Foundation]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web |last=Coyne |first=Jerry |date=2011 |title=Odd Couple Science and Religion Can't Cohabit |url=https://ffrf.org/outreach/awards/emperor-has-no-clothes-award/item/12000-2011-jerry-coyne-evolutionary-biologist |access-date=June 8, 2019 |website=Freedom from Religion Foundation |archive-date=June 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609012421/https://ffrf.org/outreach/awards/emperor-has-no-clothes-award/item/12000-2011-jerry-coyne-evolutionary-biologist |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Coyne has served as Vice President (1996) and President (2011) of the [[Society for the Study of Evolution]]. He has been associate editor of the publications ''[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]]'' (1985–1988; 1994–2000) and ''[[The American Naturalist]]'' (1990–1993). He has taught [[evolutionary biology]], [[speciation]], [[genetic analysis]], social issues and scientific knowledge, scientific speaking and writing.{{citation needed|date=August 2015}} He considers evolutionary biology to be "... more like the fine arts of science, in that it's aesthetically quite satisfying, but it also happens to be true, which is an extra bonus."<ref name="Maroon2018" />

His writing has been published in the scientific journals ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', and ''[[Science (journal)|Science]],'' as well as news and magazine publications including ''[[The New York Times]]'', the ''[[Times Literary Supplement]]'', and ''[[The New Republic]]''. His research interests include population and evolutionary genetics, [[speciation]], ecological and [[quantitative genetics]], [[chromosome]] evolution, and [[sperm competition]].

Coyne was a consultant for the defense during the [[murder trial of O. J. Simpson]] and expressed concerns that the [[DNA evidence in the O. J. Simpson murder case|DNA evidence implicating Simpson]] could be faulty.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Newton |first1=Jim |last2=Rutten |first2=Tim |author-link2=Tim Rutten |last3=Weinstein |first3=Henry |date=May 14, 1995 |title=Simpson's Team to Push DNA Data as 'Irrelevant' |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-05-14-mn-571-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240421044025/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-05-14-mn-571-story.html |archive-date=April 21, 2024 |access-date=April 21, 2024 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> In 2024, shortly after Simpson's death, Coyne shared his belief that Simpson was "guilty as hell" and the verdict was "a miscarriage of justice largely due to the incompetence of the prosecution", which had caused him to refuse subsequent requests to serve as an [[expert witness]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coyne |first=Jerry |date=April 19, 2024 |title=John McWhorter: Some white Americans would applaud O. J. Simpson's acquittal today, and that would show racial progress |url=https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2024/04/19/john-mcwhorter-some-white-americans-would-applaud-o-j-simpsons-acquittal-today-and-that-would-show-racial-progress/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420023200/https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2024/04/19/john-mcwhorter-some-white-americans-would-applaud-o-j-simpsons-acquittal-today-and-that-would-show-racial-progress/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 21, 2024 |website=Why Evolution is True}}</ref>

In a 1996 critique of the theory of intelligent-design creationism, Coyne wrote a ''New Republic'' article on ''[[Of Pandas and People]]'' (a book review), which started a long history of writing on evolution and creationism.<ref name="aodpod">{{cite web|last= Smith|first= Adrian A.|title= Episode 7 Jerry Coyne|url=http://www.aodpod.com/episode-7-jerry-coyne/|publisher= Age of Discovery Podcast|access-date= February 3, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150304083759/http://www.aodpod.com/episode-7-jerry-coyne/|archive-date= March 4, 2015|url-status= dead}}</ref>

The Ecuadoran frog ''[[Atelopus coynei]]'' is named after Coyne, who collected the [[holotype]] in a swamp on a frogging trip to western [[Ecuador]] as a student in the late 1970s.<ref name="AmphibiaWeb">{{cite web |author-last=Hogan |author-first=C. Michael |date=2013 |title=Atelopus coynei: Faisanes Stubfoot Toad |url=https://amphibiaweb.org/species/42 |access-date=May 5, 2020 |website=AmphibiaWeb |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]]}}</ref>

== Critiques of creationism ==
Coyne is a critic of [[creationism]], [[theistic evolution]], and [[intelligent design]], which he calls "the latest [[pseudoscientific]] incarnation of religious [[creationism]], cleverly crafted by a new group of enthusiasts to circumvent recent legal restrictions."<ref>{{cite news |last=Coyne |first=Jerry |date=February 12, 2009 |title=Why Evolution Is True |url=https://www.forbes.com/2009/02/12/evolution-creation-proof-opinions-darwin_0212_jerry_coyne.html?sh=540f82693500 |access-date=November 20, 2022 |work=[[Forbes]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Coyne |first1=Jerry |date=January 21, 2009 |title=Does the Empirical Nature of Science Contradict the Revelatory Nature of Faith? |url=http://edge.org/conversation/does-the-empirical-nature-of-science-contradict-the-revelatory-nature-of-faith |access-date=August 18, 2014 |work=Edge.org |publisher=[[Edge.org|Edge Foundation, Inc.]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date=June 16, 2006 |title=Jerry Coyne – The Case Against Intelligent Design |url=http://www.pointofinquiry.org/jerry_coyne_the_case_against_intelligent_design/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623201356/http://www.pointofinquiry.org/jerry_coyne_the_case_against_intelligent_design/ |archive-date=June 23, 2018 |access-date=January 23, 2014 |website=Point of Inquiry |publisher=[[Center for Inquiry]]}}</ref><ref name="Faithreview">{{cite magazine |last=Coyne |first=Jerry |date=July 1, 2007 |title=The Faith that Dare Not Speak its Name |url=http://pondside.uchicago.edu/ee/faculty/Coyne/pdf/New_Republic_ID.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200313033732/https://pondside.uchicago.edu/ee/faculty/Coyne/pdf/New_Republic_ID.pdf |archive-date=March 13, 2020 |access-date=July 29, 2007 |magazine=[[The New Republic]]}}</ref>

== Beliefs ==

=== Atheism and skepticism ===
[[File:Dawkins-Coyne CFI Event 5-24-2017 -04110.jpg|thumb|Coyne (right) and Richard Dawkins at  [[George Washington University]] on May 24, 2017]]

Coyne considers himself a [[Jewish secularism|secular Jew]],<ref name=":2">{{cite web|last=Coyne|first=Jerry|title=Stupid religious rule #11734, and a note on my ancestry|url=https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2013/04/12/stupid-religious-rule-11734-and-a-note-on-my-ancestry/|website=whyevolutionistrue.com |publisher=Jerry Coyne|access-date=February 8, 2014|date=April 12, 2013}}</ref> and an outspoken anti-theist. As a proponent of [[New Atheism]],<ref name=":3" /> he is often cited with atheists such as [[Richard Dawkins]] and [[Sam Harris]].{{Citation needed|date=November 2022}} He supports the theses of [[metaphysical naturalism]] and the [[conflict thesis]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2018}} He claims that religion and science are fundamentally incompatible, that only rational evaluation of evidence is capable of reliably discovering the world and the way it works, and that scientists who hold religious views are only reflective of the idea, "that people can hold two conflicting notions in their heads at the same time" ([[cognitive dissonance]]). He has argued that the incompatibility of science and faith is based on irreconcilable differences in methodology, philosophy, and outcomes when they try to discern truths about the universe.<ref>{{cite book| last= Coyne| first= Jerry A.| title= Faith vs. Fact| chapter= 1| year= 2016| page=5| quote= As I'll show in the next chapter, the incompatibility [between religion and science] rests on the differences in the methodology and philosophy used in determining those truths, and the outcomes of their searches. | edition= paperback| isbn= 9780143108269|publisher= [[Penguin Books]] }}</ref>

Coyne produces a website in blog format titled ''Why Evolution Is True''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coyne|first=Jerry|title=Ceci n'est pas un blog|url=https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2012/11/29/ceci-nest-pas-un-blog/|website=whyevolutionistrue.com|access-date=January 25, 2014|date=November 29, 2012}}</ref> As of January 10, 2023, it had over 73,000 subscribers.<ref name="73k">{{cite web |last1=Coyne |first1=Jerry |title=We hit 73,000 |url=https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2021/07/10/we-hit-73000/ |website=Why evolution is true |date=July 10, 2021 |access-date=July 10, 2021}}</ref> On the blog, he has covered subjects spanning science, medical ethics, atheism, determinism, philosophy and free speech.<ref name="Maroon2018">{{cite web |last1=Harris |first1=Lee |date=February 14, 2018 |title=Meet Jerry Coyne, the University's Most Prolific and Provocative Emeritus Blogger |url=https://www.chicagomaroon.com/article/2018/2/14/meet-jerry-coyne-universitys-prolific-provocative/ |access-date=February 14, 2018 |website=[[The Chicago Maroon]]}}</ref>

Coyne is an advocate of skepticism, and has stated that "all scientific progress requires a climate of strong skepticism."<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Chopra|first=Deepak | author-link=Deepak Chopra|title=Deepak Chopra Responds to Pseudoscience Allegations. Jerry Coyne Fires Back.|url=https://newrepublic.com/article/115600/deepak-chopra-responds-pseudoscience-allegations|magazine=[[The New Republic]] |access-date=January 25, 2014|author2=Jerry A. Coyne|date=November 18, 2013}}</ref> He has participated in public forums and debates with [[theism|theists]].

Coyne offers criticism of creationists who appear closed minded by adhering to a literal Biblical view. He questions the creationist concept of animals diverging only within ''kinds'', which is in itself an admission of transitional intermediates between very different groups (i.e., whales and their terrestrial relatives) found throughout the fossil record.<ref name=newrepublic20140205>{{Cite magazine|last=Coyne|first=Jerry|title=Bill Nye Won Last Night's Creationism Debate|url=https://newrepublic.com/article/116478/bill-nye-ken-ham-debate-creationism-and-evolution-science-wins |magazine=The New Republic|access-date=February 5, 2014|date=February 5, 2014}}</ref> In a ''[[The New Republic|New Republic]]'' article, Coyne wrote that "we have many examples of transitional fossils between what anyone would consider different kinds: fish and amphibians (like Tiktaalik, which [[Bill Nye|Nye]] mentioned), between amphibians and reptiles, between reptiles and mammals, between reptiles and birds, between land animals and whales, and of course, between early and modern humans, with early fossils showing intermediacy between the features of apelike ancestors and modern humans."<ref name=newrepublic20140205/> Coyne believes that both sides of such debates between evolutionists and young earth creationists could benefit from a better understanding of the fossil record and for modern tools such as [[Isochron dating]]. He considers that the inability of creationists to address these subjects fully suggests that "religion can poison one's mind so deeply that it becomes immunized to the real truth about the cosmos."<ref name=newrepublic20140205/>

He has stated that he believes in free speech for all and does not like seeing universities cancel speakers, such as [[Steve Bannon]], because of protests, saying "I can't think of a single person I would urge the University to disinvite. Not a single person – not a white racist, not an anti-immigration person. Free speech has to defend the most odious people."<ref name=Maroon2018/>

=== Determinism ===
Coyne is a [[Hard determinism|hard determinist]].<ref name=":4" /> He came to believe in the idea of [[determinism]] after reading a paper by [[Anthony Cashmore]] on determinism and the criminal justice system. He states that recognising there is no free will makes one more empathetic and less judgmental: "A lot of politics—particularly Republican politics—is based on the supposition that people are responsible for their own lives. So, for example, people who are on welfare, or homeless people, are treated as if they could have done otherwise. They could have gotten a job, they could have gotten married and had a father for their kids. But they couldn't, because they're victims of circumstance."<ref name=Maroon2018/>

===Sex as binary===
On December 29, 2024, Coyne wrote an article for the website of the [[Freedom From Religion Foundation]] (FFRF) which argued that sex is biological and binary and that trans women were more sexually predatory than other women.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://freethoughtnow.org/biology-is-not-bigotry/ | title=Biology is not bigotry |last= Coyne |first=Jerry | date=October 12, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227095242/https://freethoughtnow.org/biology-is-not-bigotry/ |access-date=2 September 2025 | archive-date=December 27, 2024 |quote=...They argue, for example, that “Transgender people are no more likely to be sexual predators than other individuals.” Yet the facts support the opposite of this claim, at least for transgender women...}}</ref> The FFRF's presidents removed the article one day later, describing its publication as an error of judgement on their part.<ref name="Shimron">{{cite news |last1=Shimron |first1=Yonat |title=Freedom From Religion Foundation dissolves honorary board in spat over trans issues |url=https://religionnews.com/2025/01/06/freedom-from-religion-foundation-dissolves-honorary-board-in-spat-over-trans-issues/ |access-date=16 May 2025 |work=RNS |date=6 January 2025}}</ref> Coyne resigned from the board of honorary members in response.<ref>{{cite web | last=Coyne |first=Jerry | url=https://whyevolutionistrue.com/2024/12/29/i-resign-from-the-freedom-from-religion-foundation/ | title=I resign from the Freedom from Religion Foundation | date=December 29, 2024 }}</ref> His resignation was followed by those of [[Steven Pinker]] and [[Richard Dawkins]], after which the FFRF dissolved the honorary board.<ref name="Shimron"/><ref>{{cite web| last= Henderson| first= Cameron| title= Richard Dawkins quits atheism foundation for backing transgender 'religion'| url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2024/12/30/richard-dawkins-quits-atheism-foundation-over-trans-rights/ | date= 30 December 2024| work= [[The Daily Telegraph]]| accessdate= 31 December 2024| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241231024341/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2024/12/30/richard-dawkins-quits-atheism-foundation-over-trans-rights/ | archive-date=December 31, 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
According to an article in ''[[The Chicago Maroon]]'', Coyne retired in 2015 and continues to pursue publishing and work in his lab at the university.<ref name=Maroon2018/> He considers himself to be a traditional liberal while also strongly supporting free speech.<ref name="Maroon2018" />

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Coyne requested permission to access the University of Chicago's Botany Pond to feed a female duck and her ducklings in the event of a campus lockdown; he had named the mother Honey, and fed the group until they migrated. The university granted his request. Honey has returned for several years to the pond, and Coyne has persisted with feeding the ducks breeding there.<ref>{{cite news| last= Schmich| first= Mary|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/columns/mary-schmich/ct-coronavirus-university-of-chicago-duck-honey-20200331-36a64jefszar3d35yc34leozma-story.html| title= Column: The pandemic, a professor and a duck named Honey: A story of life in a time of death| date= March 31, 2020| work= [[Chicago Tribune]]| access-date= May 10, 2020 }}</ref>
